text:
Kevin H: hi everyone, day 1 here. i merged the onboarding kubeconfig and switched to `redwood-dev` but when i try `kubectl get pods -n rl-search` i get `Forbidden`. not sure who to ping for RBAC. any quick way to check what's wrong?
Lina (DevEx): welcome Kevin! can you paste `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n rl-search`? also are you using the Okta exec flow or a service account token?
Kevin H: current context: `redwood-dev-cluster`. `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n rl-search` -> `no`. i used the onboarding SSO link.
Lina (DevEx): sounds like identity sync didn't map you to the `team-search` group yet. two quick routes: (1) request a personal dev namespace `dev-kevin` for immediate work, or (2) wait for identity sync / infra to add you to the team. which do you prefer?
Kevin H: prefer a sandbox to start running the sample search index locally. how do i request it?
Sam K: i can create `dev-kevin` and bind `edit` to your service account. what's the service account name shown in your error (if any)?
Kevin H: the `kubectl get pods` error mentions `system:serviceaccount:default:kevin-sa`.
Sam K: got it. i'll create namespace and apply a RoleBinding. infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-5333 to provision namespace `dev-kevin` and bind `edit` to `system:serviceaccount:default:kevin-sa` (ETA ~7m).
Kevin H: awesome, thanks. while we wait, any docs i should read to avoid this in future?
Lina (DevEx): check the onboarding k8s doc: https://redwood.dev/onboarding/k8s-access. quick checklist: (1) confirm context with `kubectl config current-context`, (2) run `kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource> -n <ns>`, (3) if you see a service account in the error, likely kubeconfig merged a SA entry — run `kubectl config view users -o name` and `kubectl config set-context redwood-dev --user=your-email@example.com` to switch back, (4) if auth succeeds but 403, open an INFRA ticket or request a personal namespace.
Kevin H: curious about the SA vs user thing. how does merging kubeconfigs cause that?
Lina (DevEx): when you `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/onboard kubectl config view --merge` without flattening, identical user/context names can get duplicated and the merged context might reference a CI/service-account user block. prefer `--merge --flatten > /tmp/merged` and then move the file into place. Also check `~/.kube/cache` for stale exec tokens — removing it and re-running the Okta login helps with 401s.
Kevin H: infra-bot updated: INFRA-5333 completed, namespace `dev-kevin` created. trying `kubectl get pods -n dev-kevin` now.
Kevin H: works! can see the empty namespace. deploying the sample search service next.
Sam K: FYI if you only need port-forwarding to a pod for local dev, we sometimes create a scoped Role instead of full `edit`. example role for port-forward only: ```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: portforward-role
  namespace: dev-kevin
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","pods/portforward"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch","create"]
```
then RoleBinding that to your SA keeps permissions minimal.
Kevin H: good to know, i'll use the scoped role once i'm ready to test port-forward to the local index. thanks everyone! :rocket: 
DevEx Bot: Reminder: delete personal namespaces when you finish to avoid resource sprawl. Run `kubectl delete namespace dev-kevin` or file INFRA ticket to retain it.
Kevin H: will do. appreciate the speedy help.
